title: MidJourney video seems kinda legit for 2D sprite anims
author: stuffedcrust_studios
selftext:
Being honest not sure if useable for my game as it seems like a headache to get a bunch of useable loops for different emotes for lots of different characters, and I can't seem to get it to do it without mouth movement (which would mean needing talking audio which comes with it's own list of headaches).

However! The results are surprisingly consistent and artifact free, gotta be some use cases for this somewhere!

comments.author: No_Surround_4662
comments.body: It's not really dynamic though unfortunately. It's nice, but the file sizes will suck, and you can't merge different animation sets. For example, you'd want the 'face' to have it's own system so it can react differently regardless of what the body is doing.

replies.author: MarcusBuer
replies.body: can be used as a reference for making your keyframes on an skeleton rig.

replies.author: _stevencasteel_
replies.body: Throw it into [vectorizer.ai](http://vectorizer.ai) and bam, you've got your different hand and mouth shapes in a couple of hours instead of weeks. $$$

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Looks cool, but you're gonna have a bad time with optimization. Every frame is unique, which takes a lot of space. In a YouTube video that's fine, but in a game it is not.

replies.author: gl0balist
replies.body: Is there any similar solution suitable for games?

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: No. For efficiency you need to split the image up in parts (head, arm, leg etc) and animate individually by moving the bones. You can look up Dragon Bones or 2D skeletal animation.

replies.author: IncorrectAddress
replies.body: You don't have to do this, you can just use a spritesheet, or a custom flat file animation, but it does depend on the game, you could even use FMV in some types of games if you know the timing.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Yes there are other ways. However doing the above animations with spritesheets is going to be huge as well.

replies.author: IncorrectAddress
replies.body: Well that depends, you could scale them however you like and limit frames to what ever numbers you need, and with RAM/GPU's these days you have boat loads of mem to play with.

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body: You don't use every frame, just turn it into a gif and extract the main ones for the animation.

replies.author: Toastti
replies.body: Considering some games have many hours of cutscenes and other video footage that takes up 10s of Gigabytes storing some extra frames onto a 2d animation is going to do absolutely nothing by comparison. Computers have so much storage and memory know you don't have to optimize to that much of an extent for 2d games like this.

comments.author: Top_Stranger5741
comments.body: Maybe for a character select screen?

comments.author: mrpressydepress
comments.body: Looks like it's worth a try

comments.author: No_Track1817
comments.body: I’ve had luck by converting the videos into gifs and then splitting the frames into a sprite sheet for animations.

comments.author: _stevencasteel_
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/vub51ukucw7f1.png?width=848&format=png&auto=webp&s=0c2130ac30483b2af0666e0ac8f781befd26f342

The tech is already good enough to bring these baddies to life.  Set a first and last frame and you've got yourself a perfect loop image sequence.

comments.author: IncorrectAddress
comments.body: Yeah, this looks good, at the least, it's a step in the right direction.

comments.author: massivebacon
comments.body: I think it’s actually pretty bad - it clearly does some bone/spine rigging for everything 2D, which is fine if that’s the style you want but isn’t how a lot of 2D is animated. That said, they said they are working on a niji video model, which I expect will be a LOT better at “frame animation”

comments.author: zekuden
comments.body: how to try it? i try to sign up and it doesn't let me sign up or access it

replies.author: EinArchitekt
replies.body: Alpha.midjourney.com <- you need pro subscription to create videos

comments.author: DarkJayson
comments.body: Maybe prompt it to make loops of them?

replies.author: stuffedcrust_studios
replies.body: yeah tried that and it doesn't do it. though you could probably fudge loops by taking a clip and then doubling it and reversing it (as another poster on this sub showed before).
